title: [Autour de La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois, pages 1 à 67] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (Longue Marche drafts, c. 1981). K is a field of finite type over Q, and k is the algebraic closure of Q in K. Let K̄ be an algebraic closure of K and E_{K̄|K} = Gal(K̄/K). This group sits in an extension 1 → π_{K̄|K} → E_{K̄|K} → Γ_{k̄|k} → 1, where π_{K̄|K} = π_1(Spec(K⊗_k k̄)) is the geometric part. B_K is the étale topos of Spec K (the classifying topos of E) and Π_K is the corresponding one-object profinite groupoid.

The previous page established two things. First, E_{K̄|K} has trivial centre. Second (Scholie), the groupoid Π_K is therefore determined up to equivalence, unique up to unique isomorphism, by the outer group attached to E.

This page extends that to morphisms. A homomorphism of fields K → K' of finite type over Q gives E_{K̄'|K'} → E_{K̄|K}. Its image is open, because the algebraic closure of K in K' is finite over K. An open image therefore has trivial centralizer. It follows that the morphism of topoi B_{K'} → B_K, or of groupoids Π_{K'} → Π_K, is determined up to unique 2-isomorphism by the induced homomorphism of outer profinite groups.

The underlying principle is formal. Hom(BG, BH) is the groupoid whose objects are homomorphisms f, whose arrows are conjugations, and in which Aut(f) = Centr_H(f(G)). If that centralizer is trivial, the component is discrete, so f is known 'à isomorphisme unique près' from its conjugacy class. In particular the structural morphism B_K → B_Q can be read intrinsically as a homomorphism of outer profinite groups E_K → E_Q.

Grothendieck then prefers a different route, using that the geometric group π = π_{K̄|K} itself has trivial centre. By Schreier/Eilenberg–MacLane extension theory, an extension of Γ by a centreless π is determined up to unique isomorphism (π and Γ fixed) by the outer action φ: Γ → Out(π). It is the pullback of the universal extension 1 → π → Aut(π) → Out(π) → 1, displayed as (15) on the next page.

The next page states the goal: to describe pairs (K, K̄) by triples (π, Γ, φ), 'with a faithfulness still to be examined'. This is a birational anabelian programme.
errors: Gap: the previous page's corollary proves trivial centralizers of open subgroups only for successive extensions of free profinite groups. E_{K̄|K} is not of that form, because its quotient Γ_{k̄|k} is the Galois group of a number field. The trivial-centralizer property for open subgroups of E_K, or of G_Q for the map E_K → E_Q, needs a separate argument. It is true (e.g. via Neukirch/Artin–Schreier-type results on absolute Galois groups of number fields), but it is not justified here.

For π_{K̄|K} with trdeg ≥ 2, the claim that it is a successive extension of free profinite groups requires an elementary-fibration (curve-fibration) argument at the level of function fields. This is plausible but tacit. For trdeg 1 the group is free profinite (Douady), and centreless and torsion-free as the previous page assumes.
Minor: the open-image claim needs [K'∩K̄ : K] < ∞, which holds for finite-type extensions but is not stated.

ideas.what: A morphism of classifying topoi/groupoids BG → BH with image having trivial centralizer is determined up to unique 2-isomorphism by the outer homomorphism.
ideas.modern_name: 2-categorical description of Hom(BG,BH); rigidity of morphisms of étale gerbes/groupoids
ideas.usually_credited_to: folklore (Giraud's nonabelian cohomology, SGA4 classifying topoi)
ideas.where_published: Implicit in SGA1/SGA4 and Giraud; later in the Esquisse and the letter to Faltings (1983) in the anabelian setting

ideas.what: Viewing the structural morphism Spec K → Spec Q as a homomorphism of outer profinite groups E_K → E_Q, i.e. fields as profinite outer groups/groupoids.
ideas.modern_name: Anabelian (birational) dictionary: fields of finite type ↔ absolute Galois groups up to inner automorphism
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (letter to Faltings 1983, Esquisse 1984); proved by Pop (1994), building on Neukirch–Ikeda–Iwasawa–Uchida for number fields
ideas.where_published: Letter to Faltings (1983); Esquisse d'un programme (1984); Longue Marche (1981)

ideas.what: An extension of Γ by a centreless π is determined up to unique isomorphism by the outer action Γ → Out(π), as the pullback of Aut(π) → Out(π).
ideas.modern_name: Schreier theory of extensions with centreless kernel
ideas.where_published: Standard; used in SGA1 and the Longue Marche

ideas.what: Encoding (K, K̄) by triples (π_{K̄|K}, Γ_{k̄|k}, φ) of geometric fundamental group, arithmetic Galois group and outer action, with the 'fidélité' question left open.
ideas.modern_name: Relative birational anabelian conjecture over number fields (geometric π_1 with outer Galois action)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck; proved by Pop and Mochizuki
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme; letter to Faltings; Longue Marche

deep.surprise_reason: The page sets up the standard anabelian dictionary: classifying topoi as outer groups, with centreless rigidity. All of this is formal or appears in Grothendieck's circulated texts and was later realized by Pop and Mochizuki. Nothing new is present beyond the draft's own gaps.
transcription_corrections: Line 3-4: 'ayant une image ouverte dans un [?] centralisateur[?] réduit[?] à 1, on sait de même' should read 'ayant une image ouverte, donc un centralisateur réduit à 1, on sait de même'.
'Il en est[?] en particulier ainsi du' should read 'Il en est en particulier ainsi du'.
Last lines: the insertion is '(par π_{K̄|K} et Γ fixés)', with 'et Γ' written below; '!isom. unique près' sits under Γ = Γ_{K̄/K}.
